disclosures.name: TestPipeAllocations
disclosures.signature: too many allocations for io.Pipe() call:
disclosures.reason: Count-bound AllocsPerRun assert (want <= 4): Go's io.Pipe() makes four allocations, the PipeWriter and the pipe's three channels (io/pipe.go). The converted Pipe() reads a count of golib-runtime objects, Go's own unit, of 14 per run at go1.26.10 on windows and linux. A single-object channel core in golib is predicted (unmeasured) to take it to 5: Go's four plus the PipeWriter's field-reference view (`pw.of(PipeWriter.Ꮡr)`, io/pipe.cs:253).
disclosures.history: count-bound AllocsPerRun assert (want <= 4): the byte-derived shim reports allocated bytes, so Pipe() - measured 1184 bytes per call, for the two heap-boxed ends plus the pipe struct's three channels and its Mutex/Once/onceError members - can never satisfy a four-MALLOC bound whatever its allocation behavior. RELABEL 2026-09-23 (C1, as ruled at ledger 2026-09-23 03:37 O4): alloc-count-semantics -> deferred. The byte-derived-shim premise is retired: the reading is COUNT. Its plan is REC-G, not zh-box.
disclosures.reading: 14 per run on windows and linux -- go1.26.10 at d804094d7a (batch 37's tip), Release with tiering off; windows: 140 go2cs-runtime object allocations (8,320 bytes) over 10 runs, alloc-units-windows.tsv line 49 (claude/g-pass2-plan 966562828d); linux: 140 go2cs-runtime object allocations (8,320 bytes) over 10 runs, alloc-units-linux.tsv line 35 (claude/p1-alloc-reading 8d9d880ca2); both TSVs under docs/phase4/data/rebank-go1.26.10/; unit COUNT, a LOWER BOUND
disclosures.plan: docs/phase4/DESIGN-channels.md §6 (REC-G): a single-object channel core (owner R, after its S-arc), predicted 14 -> 5 = Go's own 4 (the PipeWriter box and the three channels, go1.24.13 io/pipe.go) + 1 field-ref view (`pw.of(PipeWriter.Ꮡr)`, io/pipe.cs:253), UNMEASURED. No record removes the view today (REC-G states why), so 5 against the want of 4 is a prediction, not a floor. (Plan fixed up 2026-09-23 per COORD's ACCEPT-WITH-FIXES, ledger 3942e083ad.)
